description: How much credit support will NVIDIA have extended to AI cloud partners under its new revenue-sharing / credit-support model, and does it materially raise NVIDIA's contingent obligations and credit risk?
outcome: The amount of credit support / backstop commitments NVIDIA reports backing AI cloud partners' compute procurement and the resulting credit-risk exposure.
period: NVIDIA's next annual report (FY2027 Form 10-K), expected early 2027 — set by the reason: a credit-support obligation being undertaken is tracked by its amount at the next annual report.

description: What will the CPU-to-GPU attach ratio in AI inference workloads be in 2026, as Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan says it is beginning to shift from 1 CPU to 8 GPUs toward 1 CPU to 1 GPU?
outcome: The reported CPU:GPU ratio for AI inference workloads in 2026, and whether it has moved materially from 1:8 toward 1:1.
period: 2026 calendar year — set because the item reports the shift is beginning as of mid-2026 and gives no specific release date.

description: Will NVIDIA's Vera Rubin next-generation AI chip platform, the product line that carries its data center value, begin shipping by a check date (end of calendar 2026)?
outcome: Confirmation that first Vera Rubin shipments have begun, versus slipping into 2027 or later.
period: First shipments by end of calendar 2026 — set by the item: the platform 'could begin shipping later this year' in an article dated 2 July 2026.

description: How many advanced AI accelerators will Huawei, together with its chipmaking partner SMIC, produce in calendar 2026 (combined Huawei-designed Ascend output: 910B, 910C and the new 950PR line)?
outcome: The combined 2026 output of Huawei-designed AI chips manufactured at SMIC, in units, measured against the contested estimates in circulation (Nvidia's report: SMIC above 700,000 Ascend 910C by end-2026 at a 50,000-per-month run rate and several million 910B in 2027; Commerce Secretary Lutnick: 200,000 advanced chips for 2025; Chris McGuire: 800,000 910C in 2025, 2 million in 2026 and 4 million in 2027 as stress cases).
period: Calendar 2026 — set by the item's SMIC capacity figures ('by the end of this year ... 50,000 of these chips per month').

description: Will Nvidia actually resume selling H200 AI chips into China by Nvidia's FY2027 year-end — i.e., will Beijing permit Chinese commercial users to buy the chips the U.S. cleared for export in December 2025?
outcome: Whether H200 sales to Chinese customers take place (China data-center revenue returning above zero) versus Beijing keeping Nvidia locked out despite the U.S. approval.
period: Nvidia's FY2027 year-end (late January 2027) — set by the reason: a pending regulatory decision is tracked to the current fiscal year-end.

description: What will the big four AI hyperscalers' combined data center capital expenditures be in calendar 2027, and will they approach the roughly $1 trillion level Nvidia projects for next year?
outcome: The combined 2027 data center capex of the big four AI hyperscalers, measured against Nvidia's ~$1 trillion projection and the 2026 level of ~$650 billion.
period: Calendar 2027 — set by the item: Nvidia projects hyperscaler capex could reach $1 trillion 'next year' in an article dated 4 July 2026.

description: Will Nvidia's Kyber NVL144 rack-scale architecture — the rack system that houses its Rubin Ultra generation, the generation after Vera Rubin — reach first shipments in 2028, after SemiAnalysis reported the program has slipped more than 12 months from a planned 2027 debut?
outcome: First shipments of the Kyber NVL144 rack system (Rubin Ultra generation) in 2028 versus the original 2027 schedule, and whether the larger NVL576 multi-rack system ships in volume at all.
period: First shipments by end of calendar 2028 — set by the item: SemiAnalysis says the Kyber NVL144 architecture 'has been delayed to 2028' from a planned 2027 debut alongside Rubin Ultra.

description: How large will NVIDIA's supply/purchase commitments (its obligations to buy components and locked-in capacity) be at its next annual report, and is the ~$119 billion level cited in this item growing faster than the revenue those commitments support?
outcome: The dollar amount of NVIDIA's supply/purchase commitments disclosed at its next annual report, measured against the ~$119 billion cited in this item.
period: NVIDIA's next annual report (FY2027 Form 10-K), expected early 2027 — set by the reason: an obligation already undertaken is tracked by its amount at the next annual report.

description: Will the French competition authority conclude its antitrust investigation into Nvidia's cloud-AI and GPU practices with an adverse decision, fine or remedy, and by when?
outcome: The French competition authority's conclusion of its antitrust probe into Nvidia's alleged anti-competitive conduct in cloud-AI and GPU markets, including the decision date, finding and any fine or remedy imposed.
period: Nvidia's FY2027 year-end (late January 2027) — set because a pending regulatory decision is tracked to the current fiscal year-end; the item reports the probe is 'nearing a conclusion.'

description: How much new high-bandwidth memory (HBM) production capacity will SK Hynix, Micron and Samsung bring online in calendar 2027, and will it arrive early enough to ease the current HBM shortage and record prices that gate NVIDIA's GPU output?
outcome: The combined new HBM capacity the three producers add in 2027 and whether any of it arrives before late 2027, easing the shortage; measured against the item's forecast that no new HBM supply arrives before late 2027.
period: Calendar 2027 — set by the item's forecast that 'None of that supply, though, arrives before late 2027,' which places the supply-easing question in 2027.

description: Will custom ASIC AI accelerators designed by Broadcom and Marvell take a growing share of the big four hyperscalers' AI accelerator spending in calendar 2027, at Nvidia's expense, given their lower cost per gigawatt?
outcome: The split of big-four hyperscaler 2027 AI accelerator spending (and of the 19.5 GW of incremental compute capacity projected for 2027) between custom ASIC racks and Nvidia GPU racks, measured against the item's cost-per-gigawatt estimates of $6–11 billion for Broadcom/Marvell ASIC racks versus roughly $19 billion for Nvidia GB300-based racks and $25 billion under Vera Rubin.
period: Calendar 2027 — set by the item: Morgan Stanley forecasts the big four will spend over $1 trillion on AI infrastructure 'next year' and add 19.5 GW of capacity, the period in which the ASIC-versus-GPU mix plays out.

description: How far will the US crackdown on advanced AI-chip exports to third countries escalate — will the US Commerce Department go beyond its May 2026 guidance and impose formal licensing requirements or other escalated restrictions on AI-chip shipments to third countries such as Malaysia, Singapore and Japan by Nvidia's FY2027 year-end?
outcome: Whether the US Commerce Department / Bureau of Industry and Security moves beyond its May 2026 guidance to a binding export-licensing rule or other escalated restriction on AI-chip shipments to third countries, and the resulting constraint on Nvidia's sales to those markets.
period: Nvidia's FY2027 year-end (late January 2027) — set by the reason: a pending regulatory decision is tracked to the current fiscal year-end.
